question: A can do 33 (1)/(3) \% of a work in 10 days, and B can do 20% of the same work in 9 days. They worked together for 8 days. C alone completed 30% of the remaining work in 10 days. A and C together can do the same work in
solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A to do 33 (1)/(3) \% of a piece of work = 10 days 

Time taken by B to do 20% of the same work = 9 days 

**Formula used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time 

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 1 unit. 

Time taken by A to do 100% of the work = 10 × 3 = 30 days 

Time taken by B to do 100% of the work = 9 × 5 = 45 days

One day work of A = 1/30 

⇒ Work done by A in 8 days = 8/30 

One day work of B = 1/45 

⇒ Work done by B in 8 days = 8/45 

Remaining work = (1 - 8/30 - 8/45)

⇒ (90 - 24 - 16)/90 = 50/90

30% of the remaining work to be done by C in 10 days. 

∴ One day work efficiency of C = (50/90 × 30/100)/10 = 1/6 

⇒ 1/60 

One day work efficiency of A and C = (1/30 + 1/60) = 1/20 

**∴ Time taken by A and C to do the same work = 1/(1/20) **

**⇒ 20 days **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** By LCM Method

Formula used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time 

**Calculation:**

Let total work be the LCM of time taken by A and B to do the work. 

Time taken by A to do 100% of the work = 10 × 3 = 30 days 

Time taken by B to do 100% of the work = 9 × 5 = 45 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cde91175027a281074c2e9ac6aef0d3c8a306b8ffe2a40bd16e8a6fe4a67739a.png] 

Work done in 8 days = 8 × ( 3 + 2) = 40 

Remaining work = 90 - 40 = 50 

Work to be done by C in 10 days = 50 × 30/100 = 15 

⇒ One day efficiency of C = 15/10 = 1.5 

One day efficiency of A and C = (3 + 1.5) = 4.5 

**∴ Time taken by A and C to do the enitre work = 90/4.5 = 20 days **
